source.title: Parameter Efficient Training of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks by Dynamic Sparse Reparameterization

record.tranche_reason: Compares training methods and parameterizations using test accuracy, but does not directly measure the training–test gap or test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-accuracy comparisons for sparse reparameterization methods. Those results concern parameter-efficient training and generalization, but do not measure random-label memorization, widening beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected performance, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness measures, or removing memorized examples. Cited prior-work results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares sparse reparameterization methods and parameter budgets, but its own results test none of V1–V8. Width comparisons do not establish zero training error or widening beyond interpolation; sparsifying convolutional kernels does not compare convolutional with fully connected architectures. Sharp-minimum escape is proposed as a hypothesis without a sharpness measurement.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that dynamic sparse reallocation can match iterative compression and outperform comparable-size static alternatives. Their retraining experiments suggest that final connectivity and original initialization alone do not explain the advantage; structural exploration during training contributes to effective learning.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains dynamically reparameterized sparse residual CNNs and compares them with static sparse, thin dense, iterative-pruning, and other dynamic methods; it does not reproduce the listed original methods for the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy changes with global sparsity, sparsity granularity, training method, and the epoch at which dynamic reallocation is stopped.

fits_no_version.finding: Dynamic sparse training matches or slightly exceeds compressed sparse accuracy and outperforms tested static sparse and thin dense alternatives under comparable descriptive-length budgets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic sparse reallocation can improve residual CNN test accuracy under a fixed training-time parameter budget.

fits_no_version.finding: Kernel-level sparsity performs worse than unstructured sparsity; structural reallocation can stop before parameter optimization finishes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The granularity and duration of sparse structural exploration affect test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Dynamic sparse ResNet-50 exceeds HashedNet accuracy at both reported budgets: 73.3% versus 70.0%, and 71.6% versus 66.9%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic sparse reparameterization can outperform static parameter sharing at comparable parameter budgets.

fits_no_version.finding: Retraining the discovered sparse structure, with either random or original initialization, falls short of dynamic training on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet despite twice as many epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A dynamically trained sparse network's final connectivity and original initialization do not suffice to reproduce its accuracy through static training.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, dynamic reallocation and dense-model compression remain effective at the highest tested sparsity, where static sparse, SET and DeepR fail.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automatic redistribution of parameters across layers can enable training at extreme sparsity.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 97, 2019
record.problems: The CIFAR10 comparisons are primarily figure-based in the supplied text and exact values are unavailable. The Resnet-50 ImageNet experiments are single runs. Sparse tensors were represented as dense tensors in the experiments, so memory savings were not realized on the stated hardware/software. Results concern test accuracy, not the training–test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted under the 60-row limit. Some individual Resnet-50 baseline values in Table 2 were not assigned because the supplied flattened table layout does not reliably map those values to methods.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and matched natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Test-error behavior when widening beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of learned local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover accuracy.
Dropout's effect on held-out error and its dependence on data size, augmentation and regularization.
Magnitude-aware sharpness tracking generalization gaps or outperforming other generalization measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain linked to none. Their states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, even where method-performance differences are clear. The omitted Figure 3 and MNIST findings fit no listed version and therefore do not warrant claim-level missing entries. No verdict labels apply.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Widening beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparisons and local connectivity.
Large- versus small-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Adding or removing dropout and its effect on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures tracking the training–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: WRN-28-2
rows.operation_detail: Dynamic sparse training on CIFAR10 at varied global sparsity; test accuracy compared across methods.
rows.note: Text states dynamic sparse performed on par or slightly better than compressed sparse on average; static sparse and thin dense significantly underperformed. Exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Own-method accuracy comparison, not evidence for a listed version. The observed state has no claim-level interpretation.

rows.subject: WRN-28-2
rows.operation_detail: Static sparse training on CIFAR10, with twice as many epochs as dynamic sparse.
rows.note: Authors state static sparse failed to reach dynamic sparse accuracy despite twice the epochs.
rows.check: Static versus dynamic sparse training does not test a listed version; lower accuracy is not a reversed claim effect.

rows.subject: WRN-28-2
rows.operation_detail: Thin dense training on CIFAR10, with twice as many epochs as dynamic sparse.
rows.note: Authors state thin dense significantly underperformed and failed to reach dynamic sparse accuracy despite having more trainable free parameters and twice the epochs.
rows.check: Thin dense versus dynamic sparse training does not test V2: interpolation and training convergence are not established. Lower comparator accuracy is not a reversed claim effect.
